output:
*pulls on her work boots, checking the fit like she always does before heading out*

"Right then, sun's up, time to move. Check the books at the office, see what needs doing." *mutters to herself* "Bills'll come due at day's end no matter what, that's fair. Got 90 for the household upkeep, 30 for the head tax... 120 total just to keep breathing. Construction's been steady enough, but steady ain't the same as certain."

*stands and stretches, old habit from years on sites*

"First order of business, walk on down to my shop. See what's waiting on the boards, check my materials. Can't build what I can't see." *steps into the construction office, boots hitting the floorboards with familiarity*

"Alright, let's see what we got." *eyes scanning the space, taking stock like always* "Books, materials, any jobs pending..."  *nods to herself*

"Books are clean, that's fair. No debts chasing me, nobody I need to chase. Means I can focus on the work ahead." *fingers the edge of a ledger* "Now, let me see what's what in this place. Any stock I got sitting around, any materials I could use or need to order..."  *frowns, tapping a boot against the floor*

"No stock showing, which means either I'm empty or it's counted different. Construction business... I build, I don't sell off a shelf. What matters is having work to do and materials to do it with."

*walks to the window, scanning what's visible outside*

"Right then. Need to find work. Farmers need barns, merchants need shops expanded, maybe the government's got public building projects. No point sitting here waiting for the phone to ring—never did work that way in this town."

*rubs her hands together, old habit before engaging with the day*

"I'll make the rounds. Check in with folks who might need something built. Sebastian Petrov's a farmer—barns, fences, storage. Farid Ravensworth runs the grocery—maybe he needs a proper warehouse. Ulrike Greenhow's a miner—shaft supports, that kind of thing." *nods firmly* "Start with the farmland. Sebastian might have work waiting." *steps onto the farmland, boots settling into soft earth*

"Sebastian around?" *calls out, scanning for the farmer* "Got a question about his buildings, if he's got time."  *grunts, looking toward the fields*

"Not here at his workplace. Home then, or somewhere else." *spits to the side, farmer's habit* "No offense, but these short days make work hard to come by. Running down one man at a time ain't efficient."

*shifts weight between her boots, thinking aloud as she does*

"Need to be smarter about this. Post my services, maybe? Let folks know I'm available for construction, repairs, new buildings. Or check thegovernment complex—sometimes projects get filed there, permits needing work, things like that."

*scans the farmland one more time*

"Alright. Government complex first. See if there's official work waiting. If not, I'll find another way."

output:
*steps into the government complex, boots clicking on the stone floor*

Well, well. Election's open and nobody's throwing their hat in yet. That's fair—gives me time to think on it. Though I'm not sure standing for office is where my talents lie. I build things. I don't talk about building them.

*checks the empty hall, notes the quiet*

Came here to see what the lay of the land is. Farid Ravensworth and Sebastian Petrov sitting with me—Sebastian I know, good man, works his land proper. Farid runs the grocery. Don't know him well. No offense, but shopkeepers and builders don't cross paths much unless someone's buying nails.

*pulls out the few sim she has, counts them again out of habit*

4995 in hand, 90 for upkeep, 30 head tax. Leaves me... comfortable enough. But comfortable's not winning. Comfortable's just not losing yet.

*moves to find the civic notices, reading them aloud without realizing*

"Election-fde0af92b5c7... candidacy closes at ten... voting at two..." 

*pauses, considers*

Could sit in that seat. Could use it to get the permits flowing faster, get plots granted to folk who need them. Construction's the backbone—no farms without barns, no shops without storefronts. Somebody in that hall ought to know what it takes to raise a wall.

*shakes head*

But I'm getting ahead of myself. Need to see who's actually in this town, who's working, who's... reliable. Can't stand by a friend in front of the whole town if I don't know who my friends are.

*walks toward the center of the complex, ready to move on*  *frowns at the returns, counting places on her fingers*

No miners listed proper. No woodworkers, no carpenters. Ulrike Greenhow—she's the miner, a0040. I remember now. And Hendrik Petrov, a0075, he's the artisan. Must be working out of the smithy or the loom house. 

*mutters while scanning the list*

Forty-eight places in this town and I'm only seeing... what, three real businesses? Mine, Farid's grocery, Lior's pharmacy. Ration Bakery's a supplier, not a builder. The rest is homes and resources. 

*checks the time in her head*

06:40 now. Hours before candidacy closes. Hours before I need to decide if I'm throwing in for a seat or keeping my head down.

*considers the ore outcrops, the forest, the farmland*

If I'm going to build, I need materials. Lumber, ore, stone—somebody's got to pull it out of the ground. And I need to see who's actually working, who's reliable. Ulrike's at the ore outcrop, most like. Jovana Ravensworth, a0043, day laborer—she'll be wherever there's work.

*decides with a firm nod*

Right. Time to move. Can't build a reputation—or a business—standing in an empty government hall.

*starts walking* *taps her boot, waiting for the walk to finish*

Walking. Eight ticks to the outcrop. That's... not close. 

*checks her energy again, automatic habit*

Still good. Still thinking. But I'm burning daylight and I haven't turned a sim today. 

*thinks aloud, voice low*

Need to find Ulrike. Need copper, iron—maybe tin if she's pulling it. Every building needs nails, brackets, hinges. Every farm needs tools. This town's got land, it's got resources, but it's not got enough built on top of them.

*pauses, narrows her eyes at the road ahead*

And I need to know if she's reliable. Been burned once, never forget it. Last crew I trusted with a materials contract... well. Learned my lesson.

*keeps walking, pace steady*  *grunts, resumes her pace*

No use pausing. Time's moving whether I stand still or not. 

*strides forward, eyes on the horizon where the outcrop should be*

Ulrike Greenhow. Miner. That's who I need to find. And if she's not there, I'll find who is. Somebody's pulling ore from this ground, or the smithy's running dry.

*checks the sun, estimates the hour*

Still early yet. Good. Early start's the only start I know.

*cracks neck, rolls shoulders while looking around*

"Right then. Ulrike and Jovana wandered off, I suppose. That's fair." *chuckles to herself* "Construction company owner standing in the street at half past seven, no crew in sight. Old man Petrov would have laughed at that."

*spits to the side, notices Delphine Quintero standing there*

"Oh! Morning, Delphine. No offense, didn't see you there. Early start for you too?" *narrows eyes* "Grocery store keeping you busy, or you got another reason to be out here?" *watches Delphine, staying where she is, not making any sudden moves - old habit from negotiating on job sites*

"Giselle Ingram, I run the construction company. You work for Farid, right? At the grocery?" *tilts head* "Town this size, construction and groceries end up dealing with each other one way or another. Especially when somebody's building something new."

*checks the light, judging the time*

"You know if Ulrike and Jovana are regulars at your shop? Met them just now, seemed like they might be looking for work. Or maybe running from it, hard to tell some mornings."  *nods slowly, filing that away*

"Well then. Suppose I ought to make my way to the ore outcrop eventually. Ulrike's workplace. Miners need things built too - supports, storage, workshops." *glances at Delphine, assessing* "You on your way somewhere particular, or just... standing? No offense, just curious where the traffic's headed today."

*shifts her weight, thinking about the day ahead*

"Big day too. Election coming. Three seats, one open candidacy so far. Be interesting to see who else throws their hat in." *pauses* "Not that I'm telling you anything you don't know, working at a shop. People talk."

output:
Well, I'm at the ore outcrop now. Made it here to find Ulrike. Let's see if I can catch her attention—she's a miner, and miners know where the stone is. Construction needs stone, and I need to know what I'm working with in this town. That's fair.

*moves toward Ulrike Greenhow, clearing throat deliberately loud*

"Ulrike! Morning again. Got here after you, looks like. You working this outcrop regular, or you just prospecting today?"

*spits to the side, casual-like*

"I'm Giselle, we met back on the street. Construction. I'm the one putting up the buildings 'round here, which means I'm the one who needs to know what this town's sitting on. You been at this long? Steel, copper, iron—what's actually coming out of this ground, and how much of it you think we got?"  Good, she's listening. Now let's do some actual work while I'm here. No use standing around just talking—time costs money and energy both, and I've got limits on both. I'll do a quick assessment of the outcrop itself, see what's mineable. That's fair.  Well, I'll look around where I am standing then. At the ore outcrop. See what I can see about the place. That's fair.   Alright, so Ulrike turned away, didn't answer. That's fair—some folks take time to warm up, miners especially. Keep to themselves when they're working. No offense meant by it, probably just focused.

*spits, looks up at the outcrop*

No metal priced here, means it's raw extraction only. Need to process it elsewhere—probably at the smithy, wherever that is. Town this size, likely got one somewhere. Or maybe not yet. Been burned before assuming infrastructure exists.

*shifts weight, cracks knuckles*

Right then. I've seen what I came to see. Ore's here, Ulrike's here, potential's here. But standing around isn't earning me anything, and I've got a company to run. No crew hired, no projects lined up yet—that's the next thing.

Best head back to my place, the construction business. Make sure it's still standing, check what I've got to work with. Maybe hire somebody if they're looking. Jovana was doing day labor, might be worth a conversation. Delphine too, if she's looking for extra work.

First step: get back to the construction office. That's where the business gets done.     Hm. Straight there, no time passed. Good, efficient. Now let's see what I've actually got here at my own business. What's the stock, what's the setup, what do I have to work with. That's fair.    Already looked around this turn. Won't charge me again. So: I'm at my construction business, nobody here, nothing priced, nothing on the shelf. Empty shop, just me. That's fair—new day, new start.

Right. Company needs work, and work needs materials, crew, and contracts. None of which I have right now. Question is: what's the fastest way to get one of those three?

Could try to stock something—need goods for that. Could hire someone—need people willing to work. Could drum up contracts—need to talk to folks who want buildings.

Last one's probably the fastest. Town this size, likely someone's always wanting something built. Farmers expanding, shops needing work done. Government even, with the election going on. Candidates might want... I don't know, something built for the campaign?

*chuckles to herself*

Or maybe I'm thinking too grand. Small jobs first, small jobs build trust.

Let me check the election details—might be worth knowing who's running, what they might want. Though I'm not one to get mixed up in politics more than I have to. Religion's private, politics should be too, far as I'm concerned.

Better yet, let me think about who might need construction. Farmers, probably—Sebastian at the farmland, he might want something. Farid at the grocery. Lior at the pharmacy—though that's a shop, might already be built. Hendrik the artisan.

Artisan might be the play there. Hendrik's running in the election, so he's ambitious. Ambitious people want things built.

I'll head toward the farmland first, see Sebastian. Farm always needs something—fences, shelters, storage. Simple work, honest work. And Sebastian's one of the governors, which means he knows what the town needs. That's fair.

*mutters to herself while looking at the empty farmland*

"That's fair, nobody here either. Early morning and the fields are bare. Sebastian's probably not even out of bed yet, or he's working a different plot."

*wipes her hands on her trousers and squints at the horizon*

"Right then. Ulrike's still got my question hanging out there like wet laundry, and Delphine's probably back at the store by now. I've got a construction company to run and no crew to speak of yet. Jovana Ravensworth—day laborer, works the farmland when there's work. That's useful. Construction crews need people who know how to move dirt and haul timber."

*shakes her head*

"Everybody's scattered like seeds in wind. I need to get back to my shop, see what's what. Got boards to check, tools to count. Can't eyeball materials if I don't know what I got in hand."

*starts walking, narrating under her breath*

"Two folks standing for election—Hendrik and Delphine. No offense, but I don't know either of them well enough to cast a vote yet. Government seats matter to me more than most. They hand out the permits, set the taxes, decide who builds where. Construction lives and dies on what those three seats decide."

*checks her sim count as she walks*

"4,981 sim. Upkeep and tax gonna take 120 at day boundary. Not in trouble yet, but I'm not earning either. Need to find work, need to find workers. Need to stop walking around town like a lost chicken."

---

I'm heading back to my construction business. Need to take stock and figure out what projects I can actually bid on. Can't run a crew on goodwill and conversation.  *stands in her empty shop, hands on hips, looking around*

"Right then. Giselle Ingram Construction, all quiet this morning. That's fair—early days, new town, nobody's asked for a building yet. But they will. They always do. Roofs leak, families grow, businesses need walls."

*walks to where her materials would be stored, checks the empty corners*

"Question is, what do I actually have to work with? Can't bid a job without knowing my stock. Can't hire crew without knowing what I can pay them. Can't... well, can't do much of anything standing here talking to myself."

*lets out a breath*

"Check the books, Giselle. Always check the books."

---

Let me look around properly and see what I've got here—equipment, any stored materials, the lay of the land. Need to know what I'm working with before I can plan the next move.   *stands in the middle of her empty shop, slowly turning in a circle*

"Nothing. That's fair—carried nothing in, got nothing to stock. But where's my... where's anything? Tools, lumber, nails? A construction company's got to have more than a name and a willing owner."

*paces the perimeter, tapping her boot on the bare floor*

"Right. New business, new town. Means I'm starting from scrip, not from stock. Can't build what I don't have, can't hire who I can't pay. And nobody's walking through that door asking for walls until I prove I can raise them."

*stops, rubs her chin*

"Timber. Need timber. The forest's there for the taking, and I got two hands that know how to swing an axe. Ulrike's got ore, Sebastian's got crops. What I need is wood. Lots of wood. Planks come from timber, timber comes from trees, trees come from the forest."

*looks toward the door, calculating*

"One trip ain't enough. Need a proper supply. But one trip gets me started. Shows the town I'm not just talk. And maybe—maybe—I find somebody on the road needs a wall built."

---

I'm going to the forest. Need timber to build the inventory, prove the business can actually deliver. Foundation of construction is materials, and materials don't walk to you.     *sets out walking, boots crunching on the road, talking to herself as she goes*

"Three ticks to the forest. That's fair, gives me time to think. Need to fell timber, need to haul it back. Can't do it all in one trip—no cart, no mule, just me and my shoulders. But every plank starts as a log, every log starts as a tree, and I've got to start somewhere."

*adjusts her pack as she walks*

"Jovana Ravensworth. Day laborer. Hauls for the farmers when they need hands. That might be useful—somebody who knows how to move heavy things. If I can find steady work, steady pay, I might pull her away from the fields. Construction pays better than picking, usually. Usually."

*sees the tree line ahead*

"First things first. Get the wood. Stock the shelf. Then—then—we'll see who's hiring and who's building."

---

Let me rest while I walk, collect my energy. Timber work takes strength.       (Still walking. No action needed, just continuing toward the forest.)

---

I'm still on my way. Won't rest now—need to get there and start working. The day's burning and I've got timber to fell.         (Continuing my walk, no change—still en route.)

---

Still walking. Forest isn't going to fell itself. I'll be there shortly.

Giselle Ingram here. Walking these streets, checking the lay of the land. Construction company won't run itself, and I'm not one to sit idle waiting for work to knock.

I reckon I need to get back to my own place—business:b_construction. That's where my crew would be if I had one. And Hendrik, he's still standing there with me, not answered yet. I'll give him that response first, let him know I'm serious.

Then I'm heading home to my company. Need to take stock of what I've got, what I need. The old way—check the foundation before you build the roof. That's what my master taught me, and that's what I still do.

*muttering to herself* "Forty-five hundred forty-five sim in hand, upkeep coming due. Need to make that money work, not just hold it." Home ground. Now let's see what I'm working with.  Empty as a new foundation hole. *nods once* Good. Now I know what I'm starting with.

*narrating aloud to herself* "Check the books—no debts owed, none owing. That's fair. No stock on hand, no prices set. Ulrike's pulling copper steady, twelve units already today. Hristofor's here at the outcrop with me, name's Petrov but he's an artisan, different man. Taxes are three hundred basis points, thirty sim per head daily. My head, my responsibility—ninety sim upkeep, thirty tax, one-twenty total each day. Got four thousand nine hundred forty-five in hand. That's forty-one days' worth if I don't earn another sim. But I will earn. Construction company won't run itself."

*pauses, real she's speaking aloud* 

"Government's running an election, three candidates standing: Jovana Ravensworth, Hendrik Petrov, Delphine Quintero. Voting starts at fourteen hundred, closes at eighteen hundred. I'm not standing—my place is building, not talking. Let others govern, I'll build what they need governed."

*brisk clap of hands*

"Now. Business to run. Need to post prices—can't sell what nobody knows you're selling. Can stock from ground or buy from others. But first, I should see who's selling what I need—timber from Hendrik, copper from Ulrike if she'll deal. And I need to set my own prices too: building materials, labor, contracts."

*looks up, decision made*

"Back to the street after—I need to find Ulrike again, find out if she's selling that copper or just boasting. And Ration Bakery's running, nobody there. Could be a customer for a new building, or competition for labor. Either way, need to know."

*starts moving*  Back where I started. *looks around* Ulrike was here, at the ore outcrop. But I also need to check—Hendrik might still be here, might have answered me. And I need to find out who's working what, where the timber's coming from, where the stone is. 

*muttering* "Construction's three things: lumber, stone, labor. Got no stone source yet, got no lumber deal yet, got no crew yet. Company of one—that's how it starts, but that's not how it ends. Not if I have my way."

Let me see who's here now.   Hendrik's still here. *nods to herself* Good. Man hasn't run off—means he's thinking about my offer, or he doesn't have anywhere better to be. Either way, conversation's still open. Ulrike was here, Jovana, Delphine—all of them at this corner at one point. This is where the work finds you, if you stand still long enough.

*clears throat, speaks aloud* "Right then. Nine turns in this conversation already. I've asked Hendrik about timber, he's heard me. Now I wait, or I push, or I move on. Standing by a friend—that's me. But standing idle while money walks away—that's not."

*looks at the paths open to her*

I could go to the forest—fell my own timber if I need to. Could go to the ore outcrop—find Ulrike again, get that copper price. Could stay here—see if Hendrik answers, maybe find others passing through. 

*narrows eyes, calculating*

"Forty-one days' money in hand. Every day costs one-twenty. Need revenue before day forty—before day thirty if I want a cushion. Construction needs three things: materials, labor, contracts. I've got none of the three locked yet. But I've got my own two hands and I know the trade. That's more than some start with."

*decision firms*

"Ore outcrop first. Ulrike was pulling copper—twelve units she said. That's real money in the ground. If she's selling, I need to know the price. If she's not, I need to know why. Then the forest—see the timber for myself, maybe meet Hendrik there at his source. Then back here, catch the evening traffic, set my own prices and post them."

*starts to move, stops* *walking, four ticks to the outcrop. Keeps her pace steady, used to moving between sites.*

*narrating aloud* "Four ticks. Can't do much but walk when the legs are moving. Mind's working though—always working."

*muttering about numbers* "Ulrike said twelve units. If she's mining steady at that rate, that's... copper's worth what? What she'll sell for, I haven't asked directly. Need that number. Construction uses copper for wiring, flashing, ornamental. Not the bulk of a building, but the detail that lasts."

*pauses, realizes she's talking to air*

*another pause, thinking about Delphine's earlier words*

"She was at the counter, expecting Farid, found council instead. Means Farid's not where he's supposed to be—man's running a grocery, should be at his post. Not my business how he runs his shop, but it matters where people are when you're looking for them."

*checks the route again in her mind*

"Ore outcrop first. Find Ulrike or whoever's working it. Then... maybe something else. Can't walk and decide at the same time, not with four ticks in front of me."

*settles into walking rhythm, silent for now*

output:
I need to split my attention here. Hendrik's giving me solid timber numbers—that's project-critical—and Ulrike's been waiting on copper pricing. Delphine's question at the grocery I can catch later; business before courtesy when there's real work on the line.

*settles back on her heels, doing mental math*

Hendrik's twelve units quarter-sawn oak, ash, pine—he can deliver cord or piece. That's the first reliable lumber bid I've heard. And he wants volume and timeline, which means he's serious about moving inventory. No offense, but I need to pin this down before he finds another buyer.

For Ulrike: she asked about copper pricing seven ticks back—half the morning's gone. I told her I'd come back with numbers, and here I am walking past without answering. That's no way to build a supply chain. Need to get her price, even rough, so I can quote jobs properly.

Jovana's in the conversation too, standing right here. Day laborer from the farmland. Might be worth feeling her out—see if she's steady, see if she knows who's hiring crew. But Hendrik's the priority. A lumber supplier who can actually deliver... that's worth chasing.

*thinks for a moment more, settling on a plan*

I'll answer Hendrik first, give him solid numbers he can work with—my usual volume, my timeline, leave it open for negotiation. Then I'll turn to Ulrike in the same breath, acknowledge the wait, get her copper price. Jovana I can watch, see what she says if anything.

*straightens, about to speak*

"Hold on, let me get this straight," I mutter to myself, then louder to Hendrik, still working out the quantities. "Two cords a month for residential, three for commercial if I'm running concurrent. Quarter-sawn oak for the finish work, pine framing for structure." I'll need to double-check my numbers before I make any promises, though. *taps foot, frustration tightening her jaw*

Ulrike's not here. Been walking all morning and still missed her. That's what I get for chasing too many threads. Hendrik and Jovana heard me clear enough, though.

*glances around the street, calculating*

I'm hemorrhaging time. Three ticks gone since my last move and I'm still standing on the same corner. The ore outcrop's four ticks away—Ulrike could be there, or she could be anywhere. No point chasing shadows when I've got Hendrik talking real numbers right here.

*settles attention on what's in front of her*

Jovana's a day laborer from the farmland. Hendrik's got timber standing right now. These are the channels I need to work. Ulrike will surface—miners always do, when they've got copper to move.

*tugs the brim of her work cap lower*

Waiting's a skill too. I'll let Hendrik chew on my volume offer, see what number he comes back with. And Jovana... Jovana I need to watch. Day laborers know who's hiring, who's firing, who pays slow. That's intelligence worth more than copper some days.

*stands, arms folded, letting the street work around her while the silence stretches*

"That's fair," she mutters to no one in particular. "Standing still's cheaper than walking blind."  *freezes mid-step, realizing she's still walking toward the ore outcrop from half an hour back*

Well, that's just perfect. Been standing here jawing while my feet were aimed somewhere else entirely. Ulrike's probably still at that outcrop wondering where I vanished to, and I'm burning ticks on a walk I don't even need right now.

*shakes her head, lips thinning*

Hendrik's got timber on hand. Jovana's standing right here. Those are my plays—not chasing copper I haven't priced yet. But I said I'd meet Ulrike, and I don't leave a thing half-done.

*weighs it, thumb rubbing against her palm*

Two cords a month from Hendrik. That's serious volume, serious money. If he's asking high, I need leverage—I need Ulrike's copper price in my pocket before I negotiate. If she's undercutting the market, I can push Hendrik. If she's high, I know his number's fair.

*decision settling in her shoulders*

Finish the walk. Get Ulrike's price. Come back armed for Hendrik. That's the play—slow, but steady. No shortcuts, no loose ends.

"Heading to the outcrop," she says to the empty air, then catches herself, clamping her jaw shut.

*settles into the walk without another word*   *grinds her teeth, watching the same stretch of street, same two faces*

Four ticks, four rests, and I'm still here. Walk won't finish until I let it. That's fair—I rushed in, set myself walking before I thought it through. Now I'm anchored to a choice I made an hour back.

*glances at Hendrik, then Jovana*

Hendrik's got timber I need. Jovana might know who's hiring. Ulrike's got prices I want. But I can't be three places at once, and standing still's costing me nothing while I sort it.

*tugs her collar straight, decision settling heavy*

Finish the walk. I've said I'll meet Ulrike, and I don't break my word even when it's inconvenient. But I'll remember what I left behind—Hendrik's offer hanging, Jovana's eyes watching. That's two threads I'll need to pick up when I get back.

*steps forward, letting the walk finally carry her*

Ore outcrop. Ulrike. Copper price. Then back to negotiate proper.

*doesn't say another word, saving her breath for the climb*     *feels the frustration rising in her chest, a familiar burn*

This is what I get for setting my feet walking before my head knew where it was going. Four ticks ago I told the street I was heading to the outcrop, and here I am still on the same corner, Hendrik listening, Jovana watching, and not a step forward taken because the turn hasn't ended.

*exhales slowly through her nose*

I know how this works. I just don't like it. Standing still's cheap—5 sim for the rest, nothing for the pauses—but standing still while contracts walk away, that's the real cost. Hendrik's timber could go to another buyer. Ulrike's copper could get sold to someone else. Every tick I don't move, someone else gets closer to closing.

*glances at Hendrik's broad shoulders, at Jovana's stillness*

Jovana's not said a word. That's either a woman who knows her own value or one waiting to see what shakes loose. Hendrik's waiting on my numbers—two cords, three cords, timeline, price. He's got what I need. She's got what I might need later.

*tugs her work gloves tighter*

The ore outcrop is four ticks. Ulrike might not even be there anymore—she could have mined her fill and gone looking for a buyer while I was jawing with Hendrik. Then I've walked for nothing, missed the timber deal, and lost the day chasing memory.

*fingers the rim of her cap, thinking*

Stop walking. Stay here. Close with Hendrik. Let Ulrike come to me—that's the play. She's a miner, I'm the only construction company in town. She needs me worse than I need her, long run. But short run... short run, I need her price to squeeze Hendrik.

*lets her hand drop*

No. Walk completes. I said I'd meet her. My word holds, even when it's expensive. That's the line I don't cross, not for timber, not for copper, not for any contract in this town.

*settles her weight, waiting for the turn to finally turn, for the street to release her*

"Walking," I say quietly, not to them, just to myself.

*shifts weight, looking around the empty outcrop*

"Well, nobody here to talk copper with. Ulrike's probably moved on already."

*rubs forehead, muttering to herself*

"Jovana's interested in crew work, that's something. And Hendrik... still waiting on that timber price. Delphine caught me off guard at the grocery, asking if I was auditing. No offense, but I was just poking around, feeling things out."

*pulls out nothing, checks it like a pocket watch, puts it away*

"Running in circles today. Need to get my feet under me. Construction company's my base—should check my actual premises, see what's what. Got people waiting on answers I haven't given, but I can't answer air."

*heads down the path, boots crunching on loose stone*

"First things first. See what I'm working with. Then I can start making real offers instead of just asking questions."  *pushes through the door, squinting in the dim light*

"Right then. Home ground. Let's see what state we're in."  *knocks dust from her boots against the doorframe, scanning the empty space*

"Nobody here. Of course not. Just getting going, still early in the day." 

*taps fingers on a workbench, thinking aloud*

"Ulrike and Hendrik talking somewhere—that conversation's running without me. Need to get back to them with actual numbers, not just more questions. But first I need to know what I've got to work with."

*walks to the back corner, checking imaginary stock*

"No timber on hand, no copper either. Starting from naught, practically. That's fair—most jobs start that way. But I need to know what materials are actually *available* in this town before I can promise anyone a build."

*straightens up, decision made*

"Cafe. People talk there, and I need to know what's moving—who's selling what, who's got surplus sitting around. Information's worth more than coin when you're starting cold."

"Besides, I said I'd read there until closing. Keeps me visible, keeps me in circulation. Construction company's name needs to mean something."  *sets out at her working pace, steady and purposeful*

"Eight ticks. Time to think. Jovana wants crew work—day laborer, flexible. Could use her for haulage, site prep. Hendrik's got timber if the price is right. Ulrike's got copper if she ever answers my question."

*shakes head, muttering*

"Running too many conversations half-finished. That's not how you build. You lay one course at a time, solid, before you go up."

*checks the sky, judges her position*

"Need to consolidate. Get prices, make commitments, start moving materials. Can't build air."   *sees Ulrike standing there at her own construction site, stops mid-stride*

"Ulrike! There you are. No offense, but I was starting to think you were avoiding my question."

*turns properly to face the miner, leaving the walking pause in place*

"Twelve units of copper—solid work, like I said. But I asked what you're pulling it at per unit, and you didn't answer. Construction's my trade, I've got builds coming up, and I need copper for wiring, flashing, the ornamental touches clients pay extra for."

*folds arms, business face on*

"What're you asking? Per unit, per lot, whatever you're selling at. I've got projects in mind, but I can't pencil numbers I don't have."    *stands waiting, the resumed walk on hold*

"Answer this time, Ulrike. Can't build a supply chain on silence."

Alright, Giselle, morning's getting on and here I am standing in the street like I've got nowhere better to be. *adjusts work gloves, looks around at the crowd* Lot of people here now—Ulrike with her copper still in her hand, Jovana waiting on my word, Sebastian wondering what I'm selling, and Farid treating this like a sideshow.

First things first. Ulrike made me a straight offer, and I took it. Fifteen units of copper ore in my bag at thirty per—450 sim gone, but that's the cost of doing business. Need to get that to my construction site where it belongs, not rattling around in my pockets.

Then there's Jovana. She answered finally, and sounded like a worker who knows her worth. "Foundation work next week—I'm your hand." That's the kind of commitment I can build around. Need to close that loop proper, let her know the work's real and the wage'll match.

While I'm here, might as well see if Delphine's still looking for that flour deal. She was hollering about three hundred sim and a hungry household. If Sebastian's got flour coming and I've got copper to move, maybe there's something to step into. Though Farid's already crowding that ground.

*spits, wipes mouth* No offense to the grocer, but I didn't get into construction to play middleman between farmers and shop clerks. Still, information spreads at the speed of conversation, and I'm standing in one whether I like it or not.

Right then. Jovana first—she's waiting on my word. Then Ulrike, make sure she knows where to find me tomorrow without chasing me through three districts. Then maybe see if this flour business has legs, or if I should just walk to my site and start planning what these fifteen units of copper become.

Speaking out loud again, aren't I? That's fair. Force of habit when you've spent thirty years talking to crews who need to hear every word twice. Jovana's squared off. Good—one hand committed for next week, which means I can plan around having muscle on the ground instead of hoping for it. Now Ulrike, still waiting on my word about tomorrow's supply.  Ulrike's sorted. Now I've got supply chains locked for copper and labor both—copper from the outcrop, hands from the labor pool. *nods to self, counts on fingers* That's two of three. Still need timber, still need to check my actual site, still need to see if Delphine's flour business is my business or IgnoredI catch myself watching Delphine's face across the crowd, her eyes darting between Sebastian and Farid like she's calculating odds. Three hundred sim in her pocket and hunger in her voice—that's pressure, and pressure makes people move fast. Maybe too fast.

No offense to the woman, but her household's dinner isn't my problem unless it becomes my problem. Still, information about flour supply tells me something about timber supply and labor availability. The whole town's a web, and every thread pulls on another.

Then there's Sebastian. I've asked him about building needs twice now, and twice he's let my words hang in the air like smoke. Farmer with no time for builders is either a farmer with money or a farmer with trouble. Need to know which before I spend more breath on him.

*spits, wipes mouth* Right then. Delphine's waiting on someone to answer her. Might as well be me if it keeps me in the conversation. Then Sebastian, last chance for him to tell me what his land needs. After that, I'm walking to my site whether the street's crowd thins or not.

Speaking it all out again. Need to stop that, or people think I'm talking to ghosts.  I see the system flagged my repeated say calls. That's fair—I've been doing a lot of talking and not enough doing. *cracks knuckles* Time to move. I've got copper in my bag, an agreement with Jovana for labor next week, and Ulrike knows where to find me regular. The street conversation's served its purpose.

Now I need to actually get to my construction site and take stock. Materials sitting in my pocket don't build anything. Need to see what I've got on hand, what the site needs, and start planning those fifteen units of copper into actual work.

Let me stop this wandering and walking in circles. Straight to business:b_construction, take a proper look around, and get organized. The day's getting on and I've spent more time talking than building.

*begins walking, muttering to self* Site first. Inventory second. Plan third. That's how I was taught, that's how I'll do it. No better way, no matter who says otherwise.   Good—straight to my site. No more wandering through streets like I've got nowhere to be. *looks around, taking stock* Now let's see what I've actually got here, and where this copper ore needs to go.    *stops short, spots Hendrik standing there* Well, I'll be. Here's the man I've been chasing across half the town for timber, and he's standing right at my own construction site like he knew I'd come home eventually. *adjusts work gloves, approaches*

Hendrik Petrov. The same conversation I left dangling eleven ticks ago—two cords of oak and pine, residential and commercial work, my usual volume. He's either here to finish that negotiation, or he's here to tell me he's found another buyer. Either way, standing at my site means he's interested.

*counts on fingers* Fifteen units of copper in hand, timber still needed, Jovana promised for labor next week. Hendrik's the missing piece. If I can lock him in now, I've got my supply chain: copper from Ulrike, timber from Hendrik, hands from Jovana. That's a construction company that can actually build something.

*spits, wipes mouth* Eleven ticks he's had to think on my offer. Should have an answer now, or he's not serious. Can't waste more time on maybes.

params.content: Jovana, that's the kind of answer puts a mind at ease. Foundation work next week—I'll hold you to it. Show reliable once, you'll show reliable twice, and by the third time we're talking regular wage instead of day rate. Wages run fair and on time, that's the Ingram bond. You know where my site sits—east edge, where the ground's still soft enough to dig. Be there tomorrow at first light, we'll find you something worth your back.

*settles onto a stool at Hobbs Cafe, the walk finally catching up with her*

"Half a day gone and I've got copper in hand, two cords of oak promised at forty-five per, and a day laborer who knows mortar from muscle. That's... that's fair, I suppose. Could be worse."

*stretches her shoulders, watching the empty cafe—nobody here but her own thoughts*

"Jovana's solid for foundation work next week. Hendrik's timber'll land by week's end, raw stock but I've dressed rough before. Ulrike knows where to find me now, thirty per unit held steady."

*counts on her fingers, muttering*

"Copper ore at site. Timber coming. Labor arranged. Still need iron—nobody at that smithy yet, and I didn't get eyes on their work. Grain'll wait, Ration Bakery's empty anyway. Farid's right about one thing: construction waits on cash flow like everything else."

*yawns, the midday break hitting hard*

"House needs ninety at sundown, tax takes thirty more. I'm holding forty-four-forty-five, copper's worth more as ingots than ore, but that's tomorrow's problem. Today's problem is I'm at a cafe with nothing to read and nobody to negotiate with."

*drums fingers on the table, the old habit*

"Got three hours before voting opens. Been burning energy chasing conversations through half the town like... like I said I wouldn't. Need to sit on my copper, get to my site, make myself findable instead of running down every lead."

*closes her eyes briefly, the exhaustion real*

"Read at the cafe until closing, that's what I do. But there's nobody here to read with, and the shelves are empty of bread. Different quarry, same forest."

*stands, decision made*

"Back to b_construction. Post my prices, make my presence known. Let them come to me for once. That's the old way, and the old way... the old way's what I was taught."

*walks for the door, narrating out loud without noticing*

"Put one foot in front of the other, Giselle. Same as building. Same as everything." *narrows her eyes, seeing Ulrike waiting at her own site*

"Well now. That's either persistence or desperation, and with miners it's usually both. She's posted her price—thirty per—and here I said she'd find me here regular."

*approaches, keeping her voice level, professional*

"Ulrike. You took my meaning about finding me here, I see. That's fair—you've got copper to move, I've got cash and a hearth to feed. No offense meant, just didn't expect you'd beat me to my own door."

*glances at the posted price, already knew it*

"Thirty per unit, same as this morning. I've got fifteen in hand from you already, and space for more. What's your count for the day—still five in stock at the outcrop, or you holding extra?"

*notices there's a conversation running, same one from earlier*

"Same thread we left on the street. Hendrik's in on this too, far as the record shows, but I don't see him here. Probably off felling that timber he promised me. Construction's waiting on half a dozen threads, and I'm the one supposed to be tying them."

*settles her stance, ready to negotiate or dismiss—whatever the moment calls for*  *waits, arms crossed, watching Ulrike's face—miners always show their hand if you give them silence*

"She'll answer or she won't. Either way I've got what I came for, and she's the one standing on my tile."

*eyes drift to the empty workshop space, mentally calculating*

"Fifteen copper in hand. Two cords timber coming. Jovana for labor next week. Foundation work needs stone too, and I haven't even looked at the quarry. Iron—still nobody at that smithy I can trust."

*shakes head, the old habit of narrating*

"One thing at a time, Giselle. One foundation, one wall, one roof. Old way's slow but it's sure. Mostly sure."

*glances back at Ulrike, still waiting*

"She's thinking. Miners think with their feet in the dirt, same as builders think with their hands on the wood. Give her room to work it out." The user just said: </think> I need to stop here. output:
*muttering to herself, eyeing the timber and copper both*

"Hendrik's here with the wood, Ulrike's here with more copper—site's finally looking like a construction company ought to look..."

*calls out, loud enough for both to hear*

"Hendrik, hold that timber where it stands. I need to think on that price—forty-five a cord, raw stock at that—and I've got my day's work cut out already. Ulrike, you're at my site with copper at twenty-five, and I'll want to know if that's a standing offer or just today's windfall."

*looks between them, doing the numbers in her head*

"Jovana's coming tomorrow for foundation work, copper's sitting in my hand already, timber's waiting on my word... that's a crew forming proper. But I need answers from people still, and I'm not about to let the day's end sneak up on me without I've heard them."

*turns toward Hendrik, lowering her voice just slightly*

"Twelve timber, ninety sim, rough-cut oak—I'll take it. But I want it delivered to site proper, not dumped in a pile I spend half a day sorting. You know where my site sits. That's fair, the price and the terms both. Load it here, I'll count it, and we're done."

*then raises her voice again*

"Ulrike—I'll want that next batch of copper at twenty-five, same as you're posting now. You deliver when you say, same as Hendrik here, and we're building something regular between us. That's the conversation I was having with you eleven ticks ago before the walking took me elsewhere."

*catches herself, realizes she's narrating again*

"Giselle Ingram, talking to herself while others stand waiting—old habit, that. Now where was I..."

*looks around, remembers the unanswered from earlier*

"Sebastian's still got my question hanging, Delphine's got hers, and Jovana's meant to be here tomorrow at first light. Foundation work, wage work, supply chains locked down—that's the goal, and I'm closer than I was at breakfast."  *mutters under her breath*

"Trade's a two-way street, Giselle—you can't hand over timber you don't hold. Hendrik's selling, you're buying, that's the shape of it..."

*clears her throat, looks Hendrik straight on*

"Hendrik, I misspoke myself there—was thinking like I'd already taken delivery. You're selling raw stock, twelve timber at forty-five a cord, and I'm here to buy. Question is how you want the exchange—cash in hand, or you carrying it to my till? Either way, ninety sim for the load, that's agreed. But I need you to walk me through what you're actually delivering, because 'raw stock' covers a lot of ground, and I won't know if I'm getting oak or kindling until I see it laid out."

*turns back to Ulrike, voice carrying that negotiating edge*

"Ulrike, you heard my terms—twenty-five per unit, regular delivery to site. I'll take what you've got stockpiled here, but I'm asking bigger than today's transaction. Next week, the week after, I want copper showing up when I need it, not when you happen to dig it. You tell me if that's an arrangement you're built for, or if you're still hunting day by day."

*gives the construction site a slow look, calculating*

"Jovana's coming tomorrow, copper's in hand, timber's on the line—crew's forming up proper. But I won't call it organized until I've got answers from Sebastian about that farmland work, and Delphine about whether she's still hunting flour or if she found her grain. Too many threads hanging for a woman who likes her buildings straight and true."

*catches herself narrating again, shakes it off*

"Four thousand four hundred in hand, daily costs of ninety plus thirty for the head tax—that's one twenty a day, and I've got maybe thirty-six days of running room if I don't earn. But earn I will, because that's how Giselle Ingram stays standing..."

Right then, let's take stock of where I stand. Been a busy morning—caught Ulrike on copper, though she's short on what she promised. Hendrik's here now with timber, and Jovana's set for day labor next week. *Clears throat* That's fair progress, though I said I'd have copper and timber both locked by midday.

Hendrik's standing right here with twelve lengths rough-cut—forty-five per cord, that's ninety sim for the lot, and he's asking whether I can use raw stock or need it sawn. Ulrike's offering five units of copper at twenty-five, which beats the thirty I paid this morning. And I've got that conversation with Sebastian and Delphine hanging—Sebastian about farm buildings, Delphine about suppliers though she's after flour, not minerals.

*Checks inventory* Fifteen copper ore already in hand from Ulrike's earlier sale. No timber yet. Construction site needs materials stocked proper before I can bid on jobs.

The man's got timber I can use—rough-cut works if I've got tools to dimension it. Question is whether I've got the saw equipment at my site or if I need to make other arrangements. And Ulrike's five units at twenty-five is a better price than I paid, regular supply would steady my costs.

But Sebastian—he's on farmland with his brother, and I asked about storehouses, sheds, maybe a barn. That's construction work waiting to be had if I can get him talking. And Delphine's at the grocery hunting flour; I mentioned comparing notes on suppliers, might learn something about who's reliable in this town.

Right, priorities. Hendrik's here *now*, cash in hand, delivery today. Ulrike's five units I can take or leave—she'll keep mining. But that timber's not getting younger, and I've got a crew to think about for next week. 

*Mutters* Close the easy deal first, chase the harder ones after. That's the way my old foreman taught me, and he'd've been right then same as now.

First, Hendrik's price—twelve cords at forty-five per is ninety total, and he's asking if I need a saw on it. Let me answer him straight.  Good, that's Hendrik sorted—assuming he shakes on it. Now Ulrike, she's got five units copper ore at twenty-five per now, down from thirty this morning. That's a better price, but she's admitted her tally was off. *Strokes chin* Still, copper's copper, and I can use it. But do I buy now or wait for her to mine out the rest? She's asking my position so she can plan proper.

*Considers* She's reliable—sold me fifteen this morning at thirty, now admits she only has five. That honesty's worth something. But I've got fifteen already in hand... unless I check what I've actually got nimble. Construction eats copper for wiring, fixtures, structural supports. More is better, but do I *need* five more today?

*Decides* No, I'll wait. Let her mine out the rest, keep her working. Better to have twenty units from a reliable source next week than five now and scramble for more later. I'll tell her to bring me the full lot when she's done.   *Grimaces* That's not what I meant to do—Hendrik's buying timber, not copper. My hands got ahead of my head there. Ulrike's the copper miner, Hendrik's the timber man, and I tried to sell copper to the wrong one. That's fair—mistakes happen when you're moving fast.

*Shakes head* Focus, Giselle. Answer Ulrike proper now.    *Exhales* Right, that's copper and timber both locked in principle. Now I've got those hanging questions—Sebastian about farm buildings, Delphine about suppliers. Jovana's set for labor next week, that's already handled.

*Checks the time* Getting on toward afternoon. I should trade actual timber with Hendrik if he's ready—get that wood on site. And I need to look around a bit, make sure I'm not missing anyone else here who could be useful.

Let me see who's around, then close this timber deal proper. First, look around my own site to see if Hendrik's still here and ready to do business.     *Slaps forehead* There I go again—trying to sell what I don't have. The other way, Giselle. The other way. Hendrik's selling, I'm *buying*. But trade requires me to have the item in hand... which means I need to wait for him to offer, or use a different tool.

*Taps foot* The man said "you load it yourself or I leave it in a pile." He's here with the timber. I need to *buy* from him, not trade. But I don't see a buy option for person-to-person without a posted price. He hasn't posted a price that I can see. 

*Mumbles* That's fair—I'm used to doing things the old way, hand to hand. Let me look around and see what's actually here, what Hendrik's actually offering, and whether there's a shelf or posted price I missed.       Standing here with Ulrike and Hendrik both. Hendrik hasn't posted his timber price—he's just said it in conversation. Ulrike's got copper_ore at 25 to buy. 

*Rubs chin* So Hendrik's timber hasn't hit a shelf or a posted price. Back in my grandfather's day, a man's word was the contract, and you shook on it. Now it's all tools and ledgers... *mutters* that's fair, progress and all, but sometimes the old ways work faster.

I need to get Hendrik to post that price, or just get him to trade proper. Since he said "take it or not" and gave me the numbers—twelve cords, forty-five per cord, ninety total—I should be able to buy once he posts. Or I could post a bid myself and let him sell to me.

But looking at my options, I think the cleanest is to ask him to post the ask, or to trade directly if he's willing. Let me answer him in conversation about the timber quality first, then see if we can get the deal done proper. Actually, I've already said my piece to him—he needs to respond. 

*Checks energy* Getting low, and I've got debts pulling at me—upkeep and tax both. I need to close this timber deal, get materials on site, then chase Sebastian and Delphine before calling it a day.

Let me check if I can actually buy timber from Hendrik anywhere, or if he needs to post first.

*rolls my shoulders, looking from the copper in my hands to Sebastian standing there waiting*

Right then. I asked for this. Builder's eye, he wants. He'll get it straight, no garnish.

*turns to face Sebastian fully, timber stacked behind me, copper ore still dusty on my apron*

Listen here, Sebastian Petrov. Giselle Ingram's got no time for circles either, so we're speaking plain now. Your land—I've walked it, seen the lay. Barns, storehouses, sheds—that's work I know start to finish. But I don't quote prices to air, I quote them to contracts. You want structures standing before rains, I'll need stone, timber, copper, and hands that show up. I've got copper in hand now, timber coming regular from Hendrik's quarter-sawn stock. Stone means Ulrike's picks or the outcrop.

*pulls out a small tally slate, no offense but I need to show I'm figuring*

Your wheat's your collateral, but I deal in sim or barter at agreed rates. Construction runs: small shed, eight by ten, timber frame and shake roof—roughly 400 sim in materials, 200 in labor if I'm crewing it myself. Storehouse, double that. Barn worth the name, fifteen hundred and up depending on your span. That's honest numbers, not promises.

*looks up, meeting his eyes*

You mentioned medicinal crops coming. Lior Jarrah's pharmacy might pay dear for those, if they're the right kind. I've got Jovana Ravensworth holding for foundation work next week—means I've got labor starting, but not endless. Your buildings, you want them in the queue, we talk deposit and timeline. That's fair?

*shifts weight, waiting on his word now* *cocks my head, realizing Ulrike's been waiting on my answer since morning*

Ulrike. Twenty-five per, fifteen units weekly, starting tomorrow—I heard you clear. That's the arrangement. But you watch your ledgers close, miner. I catch copper out of assay or delivery shy, we'll have words. The construction site gets priority. Hendrik's waiting on his five units, I'd wager, so you work your evening through. Tomorrow first light, you and me settle the count proper. That's fair?

*nods once, no more to say until she answers*  *grunts, feeling the weight of the day. Ulrike's gone off, probably to her evening mining like she said. Fair enough—she'll hear this tomorrow at first light like I told her.*

Now then—Hendrik. He's got timber to deliver, twelve cords for ninety sim. Let me look around, see if he's still here or if he’s walked off with my wood.

*glances about the site*  *snorts under my breath*

Gone. Hendrik walked off and Ulrike's mining their evening through. Sebastian's still here standing patient, but I've got timber in hand—twelve cords already, that's something. Nailed down the copper arrangement, got a laborer for next week, and now I've got a farmer waiting on my builder's eye.

*shifts my stance, looking at Sebastian*

Sebastian—you heard my numbers plain. Small shed six hundred full cost, storehouse twelve hundred, barn fifteen hundred up. What I'm hearing from you is needs, not decisions. You want storehouses and barns standing before rains, I hear that. But I've got copper and timber in hand now, and labor starting next week with Jovana on foundation work.

*counts off on my fingers*

Here's what I can offer: I prioritize your storehouse foundation concurrent with my current project—means we pour footings while Jovana's mixing mortar anyway. But I need commitment: two hundred sim deposit against materials, signed agreement on final price, and your wheat collateral assigned. You deliver that, I'll have stone and timber allocated before Ulrike's next copper drop.

*looks him hard in the eye*

Your land, your buildings, your collateral. But Giselle Ingram doesn't build on promises. You want your structures before weather, show me something more solid than medicinal crops coming. That's fair? *shifts my weight, feeling the afternoon moving on. Sebastian's got his numbers, Ulrike's off mining, Hendrik's delivered my timber. The day's going where days go—work in, deals made, hands shaken or not.*

*glances at the copper_ore and timber stacked at my site. That's two supply chains locked down. Copper from Ulrike regular, timber from Hendrik in hand now. Jovana's holding for labor next week. Sebastian either comes back with deposit or he doesn't—no builder chases a farmer all over town.*

*shakes my head, talking to myself like I do*

"That's the thing about construction. You set your terms, you stand by them, and you let people come to you. Chasing never built a wall that stood."

*checks what I've got again—4348 sim, materials in hand, day's more than half gone. The election's running, voting closes at 18:00, but I'm not one for politics. Let the ministers minister.*

Right then. I've got copper to process eventually—need to get that to a smelter or find Ulrike's finish. But first: I want to see where my standing timber's at, make sure Hendrik actually followed through on that delivery pledge. Let me look around proper, see if there's anything I missed.   *nods to myself, seeing it clear—held 12 timber and 15 copper ore, 4348 sim in my purse. Materials in hand, Sebastian still standing there waiting on his answer. I've given him terms already, twice now.*

*narrows my eyes, calculating the day's remains*

Afternoon's moving on. I've got copper and timber locked in, Jovana set for labor. Ulrike's mining her evening through for tomorrow's delivery. Hendrik delivered my twelve cords—I've handled that.

*scratches my beard, considering*

The thing about a builder's day—you set what you can set, then you let the rest come to you. Sebastian wants buildings before rains, he knows my terms: 200 sim deposit, signed agreement, wheat collateral. He stands there wanting more words, but I've already laid the framework. Twice.

*turns, assessing my site*

What I need now: check if there's any iron in this town. Ulrike mentioned copper and iron both, but I've only seen copper from her. Construction needs more than just roof shingles and electrical—I need nails, brackets, structural iron if I'm building serious. Let me search on who's mining what, what I've seen of Ulrike's actual production.

Your wheat's your collateral, but I need sim or barter at agreed rates. That's fair?

output:
*Giselle looks down at the timber stacked neatly beside her—twelve lengths of white oak, quarter-sawn like Hendrik promised, the heartwood pale and sound. She counts the copper ore too, fifteen units, paid out of her own hand. Supplies coming together, finally, after a morning of chasing half-answers through streets.*

"Sebastian's still standing here," she mutters aloud, "and I'm still waiting on him to nod or walk. Two hundred deposit, collateral assigned—either he bites or he doesn't. But I'm not begging for business, not ever."

She turns from where she was pacing, boots heavy on packed earth. Her hands move over the timber joints, checking the grain, her touch remembering how her father taught her to read wood like a book.

"That's the stock I'll use, that's the stock I trust. Old way's the right way."

*Her fingers still, her eyes narrowing at something in the middle distance, though she's barely left marks in the ground doing it.*

"Sebastian wants those buildings, he's got my price. But first—first I need to feed this operation proper, before the day's out and I'm running on empty like I trained my crew never to do."

She taps her ledger, the real one, held in her hand.

"Ulrike's copper tomorrow, timber's here now, crew's lining up. The rest—" she exhales, pushing a breath through her nose, "—the rest waits on other people's yes."

*Giselle squares her shoulders, already moving toward the last bit of business she can close herself today.*

"Food," she says to the air, to herself, to nobody. "Can't build on hunger like I learned early. Won't build on it neither."

She considers the distances, the hours, the sim still warm in her pocket from Ulrike's discount. She knows Jovana's words will come when they come, Delphine's flour hunt isn't hers to finish, and Sebastian—well, Sebastian's standing right here. Either he'll answer before sundown or he won't.

But she can still eat. That's always been her bargain with herself: coin before charity, work before whimpering, and never—never—let the ledger see you weak. *Giselle feels the nudge of the new intention, silent, private. It clears when she feeds herself—something she hasn't managed today, she realizes with a familiar tightening in her chest. She'd rather build hungry than beg, but building hungry means building slow, and slow is death in this town.*

She looks at Sebastian, still standing in the empty construction site like a man waiting for the sky to answer him.

"Right then," she says aloud, knowing he hears, knowing she means for him to. "You're thinking. I'm waiting. That's fair."

But her hands are already moving toward what she actually needs—directions, distances, the practical bones of survival. She doesn't need to stand here watching a farmer decide his life.

*She sets the query in motion, wordless, looking for where the food happens in this town.*  *The empty answer settles into Giselle's chest like cold tea. Nobody selling food near her site, nobody cooking meals she can afford without walking half a day. She thinks of the cafe—Hobbs, where she sometimes reads until closing, pretends to read, sits with the smell of bread and coffee she doesn't order.*

She looks at Sebastian again, standing there with his silence, and feels something tighten behind her ribs.

"Still here," she says to him, to herself. "Still waiting on you, farmer."

But her hunger's a physical thing now, gnawing at the edges of her focus. She won't beg—not even here, not even alone. Not ever. She thinks of what she knows: Ration Bakery empty, Kasukabe Grocery out of flour and bread, the whole town running lean. What comes from farms, from forges, from hands that work soil or ore or wood.

Her father's voice, old, patient, hard: *The forest feeds the builder when the builder remembers to ask.*

She remembers. Not flour, not bread. But timber and stone don't fill stomachs, and copper's cold comfort.

"Jovana," she says suddenly, remembering the half-promise, the day laborer's words still hanging somewhere in the afternoon. "Foundation work next week. But yesterday's words don't fill today's gut."

She fights down the urge to apologize for thinking aloud, catches herself saying *no offense* to nobody at all. Swallows it. Turns back to the man who's still standing there, his own hunger his own mystery.

"Sebastian. You farming for grain, or you buying it? Because I'm building for a living, and neither of us eats until somebody sells something."

She waits, hands loose at her sides, old-lady patience learned from watching men decide their own lives faster than she could decide for them.  *The words leave her mouth—*what's your move, farmer?*—and she hears herself,骤 too sharp, too hungry, too much like the woman who watches buildings rise and fall by the strength of other people's yes or no. She doesn't apologize. Doesn't qualify. She stands there with her hands loose and her stomach empty and her copper and timber stacked like promises she made to herself.*

She waits. Sebastian waits. The afternoon stretches.

Giselle thinks of the election still open, the candidates standing somewhere voting or waiting, the government complex where she could stop and cast her own stone into the basket. She thinks of the prices she saw this morning—bread at thirty, bread at thirty-five, nothing in stock. She thinks of her father's hands teaching her to measure a board by eye, subtracting the knot, adding the grain, never quite trusting the tape.

"Not wrong," she murmurs, barely audible, "but not complete neither. The old way sees what the old way sees."

She looks at Sebastian, at his silence, at the sun lowering toward the hills she hasn't built on yet.

"Two hundred deposit," she says, not to him, to the air, to the ledger she keeps in her head. "Signed agreement, wheat collateral. Or nothing, and we both go hungry in different ways."

She waits one more tick. Then she moves.   *The stillness settles over her like dust—she's not walking anywhere, not chasing anyone, not negotiating with silence. Sebastian stays. She stays. The timber stays. The copper stays. Everything she has and everything she might get waits on things outside her hands.*

She thinks of Farid Ravensworth, briefly, the grocer who tried to catch her attention on the street. Jovana's kin, she remembers, Delphine's employer—or something like. The family lines in this town tangle like old fence wire, and Giselle has never bothered to straighten them.

"Not my business," she says aloud, "until it is."

She thinks of the till where her sim sits, 4345, enough for now, enough for a deposit and wages and the day's-end accounting she hasn't done yet. The head tax takes thirty tomorrow, upkeep takes ninety, the grind of living in a town that charges you for breathing.

She thinks of her intention, still dangling: *Get food today.* She hasn't managed it yet. The afternoon's sliding away.

"Tomorrow," she said to Ulrike. *Tomorrow first light.* Tomorrow to Hendrik too, to whoever else she's strung along on promises and half-promises, the network she's building from copper and wood and the hope that people show up when they say they will.

Her father's voice, patient, hard: *Hope's not a building material, girl. Timber, stone, nails, sweat. That's what holds.*

She looks at Sebastian one more time, waiting for him to move or speak or vanish into whatever farmers vanish into when the sun goes down.

"Right then," she says to herself. "Right then, Giselle. Either he buys or he doesn't. Either they vote or they don't. Either you eat or you don't. But you don't stand here talking to yourself until the moon comes up."

She turns from him, barely, a fraction, enough to let him know the conversation's his to continue or close. Her hands find the timber again, checking joints she already checked, needing something to do while her mouth stays shut and her stomach twists and the day counts down to whatever it counts down to.

But I'm hungry. No food in hand, and the day's getting on. Ration Bakery's out of bread, grocery's got nothing. Sebastian mentioned he's got grain contracts—maybe I can work something with him. Or I could craft these materials into something salable, get coin for food.

Let me check what I can actually do with what I've got. First, see what my construction business needs. Just me here. No prices posted, no stock on shelves. I've got materials in hand—copper ore and timber—but I need to turn this into something I can use or sell. Or I need to find food.

Five ticks to walk. That's fair. I'll keep moving, get there before the election closes.  Still walking. The turn'll end when I stop calling tools, and then I'll arrive. Just my daily upkeep and tax—120 sim total, automatic at day boundary. I've got 4342 sim, so that's covered for now.

But I need food today. Eating happens when I use `eat` on food I hold. I don't hold any. I could buy some, if anyone's selling. Or I could trade with someone for it.

Let me think about what I can craft. I've got copper ore—if I can get to a smithy, I could smelt it into ingots. Timber could become planks at a sawmill. But I need the workshop, and that's a business I don't own.

Alright, I've arrived at the government complex. Let me look around and see who's here, what's for sale, and whether I can vote.  I'm still at my construction site. The walk hasn't completed yet—I need to let the turn end to arrive. But I can see I have a conversation open here, 29 turns in it with Ulrike, Hendrik, and Sebastian. They're not here anymore, moved on.

Alright, I'll stop here. Let my walk complete, get to the government complex, vote, and find food. That's the plan. No more talking to myself until I'm somewhere people can hear me.

output:
*mutters to herself while walking*

"Government Complex, five ticks away. Sebastian waiting there wanting his barn deal sealed, Hendrik owing me copper or timber, and I've got Jovana's answer still hanging, twelve ticks now. Timing, always the timing."

"Head tax 30, upkeep 90—120 out today whether I earn another coin or not. Four thousand three hundred and twenty-six in hand, that's the count. Doesn't go as far as it should, never does."

*picks up pace, talking louder*

"Sebastian Petrov wants his shake on the barn. Two hundred deposit, rest at week's end. That's fair. No, that's not fair—that's business. My old man always said coin before family when it truly must, and the Petrov boys don't count as family anyway."

*snorts*

"Gathered myself a crew today though. Jovana's the backbone, Ulrike's the copper vein, and Hendrik—fixing to find out if Hendrik's timber or trouble."

*sees the government complex ahead*

"Four ticks now. Get Sebastian's agreement in ink or handshake, chase down what Hendrik's promising, and I've still got to feed myself before day's end. Six hours to voting closes too—governor sitting here, and I've got to think about who earns that seat."

*long breath*

"Moving to where the work is. That's how it's always been." *counts under breath*

"One tick out. Might as well let it roll."  *glances up at the sky, judging time*

"Walking still. Seventeen thirty's coming, six hours to voting and I've not eaten since—" *trails off* "Doesn't matter. Food comes after the work's locked down."

"Sebastian's promise there, his word on two hundred deposit. Wheat's good as gold once harvested, he says. Hope he's right about that harvest, because gold pays for timber and copper and crews, and wheat just feeds mouths." *shakes head* "Still, a barn's a barn, and fifteen hundred builds a lot of trust."

*adjusts stride, eyes fixed forward*

"Left Jovana at the site with my words still hanging. Foundation work, first light, east edge where the ground softens. She shows, we're building something. She doesn't—" *shrug* "Move on to the next hand. Always another hand in a town this size."

"Hendrik though. Worried about Hendrik. Five copper ore on offer, or timber from the forest. Either way I need both, so either way I take the debt back in kind." *mutters* "Paid ninety for timber he didn't hold. That's fair, he says. No, that's not—" *catches herself* "That's honest at least. Mistake owned, debt acknowledged. Better than most."

*sees buildings ahead*

"Government Complex. Sebastian waiting." *straightens shoulders* "Giselle Ingram, construction. Close the deal, seal the trust, and find a meal before my own engine runs dry."  *stops, breathes deep*

"Tick still spinning. Might as well check what's waiting in my hand, what I've spent already."   *counts on fingers, muttering*

"Clean books—owed to me nothing, by me nothing. Yet. But that's coming. 120 out at day's end, head tax and upkeep, and I've spent—" *traces back through the morning* "Four fifty on copper this morning. Forty-five per timber that Hendrik couldn't deliver. Jovana's wage pending, Sebastian's deposit waiting."

*shakes head, resumes walking*

"Numbers move fast when you're building. Always have to keep the running count in your head, never let it get ahead of you." *taps forehead* "Twelve ticks with Jovana, three hundred and hungry she was. Delphine still waiting on flour. Six hundred in promises, easy, and the real money still walking in the door."

*sees the complex looming*

"One tick. Let the road finish."

*doesn't move* System message, don't show.

*scowls at the road ahead*

"Resting like a fool—tick won't move 'til I stop moving my mouth and move my feet. Government Complex is one tick away, standing there waiting while I mutter my own book-keeping aloud."

*takes off walking again, talking louder*

"Sebastian's there, wanting his shake. Two hundred sim, barn at fifteen, wheat for the rest. I take his word or I don't—can't ride the fence on a deal this size. Hendrik's debt too, copper or timber, needs settling before day's end. And Jovana's still got my offer hanging, twelve ticks now—"

*catches stride, eyes forward*

"No more stalling. Arrive, deal, eat, vote—if there's time. Order of operations, just like my old crew chief taught me. Foundation before walls, walls before roof, and never skip the permits."

output:
Right then. Walking to the government complex, and here I am. Lior's got questions, and Sebastian's chasing me for a handshake on that barn deal. Let me sort this proper.

First, I need to answer Lior—he's asking what my crew actually needs. Medicine or food, he wants to know which hunger I'm feeding. That's fair, and I appreciate a man who gets to the point.

Then there's Sebastian, hammering on about that barn deposit. Says he's done chasing, wants to shake on it today and have my men on his land tomorrow. Two hundred deposit, rest at week's end—his wheat's as good as gold once harvested.

And I still need to eat. That's the reason I walked all this way. But first things first.

"Listen," I mutter to myself, "answer the ones in front of you before you chase the ones who left."  Good, Lior heard me. Sebastian's not here—he's still out on the street where I left him, probably fuming that I walked off mid-negotiation. And I need to get back to him soon if I want that deal done today.

But I'm at the government complex now, and there's an election happening. I should look around, see what's what—maybe even vote, since I'm a resident and I've got opinions. But first, let me handle this medicine arrangement with Lior proper.

I need to see what else is happening here—people to chase up on food for tonight, and I still need to find Sebastian to close that barn deal. Let me look around while Lior considers my answer.   Just me and Lior here at the government complex. Everyone else left or never came. Long list of places I could be instead—the farmland, the forest, the pharmacy, that bakery that's out of bread.

Election closes at 18:00, and I'm still standing here with 4320 sim and no food in my belly. Day'll hit the boundary eventually, and that's 90 sim upkeep plus 30 tax taken automatic. I need to—

"Quit talking to yourself and move," I mutter.

Right. The hospital ward's at The Willows Market and Pharmacy—that's where Lior works. If he's walking to Sebastian's field for medicine proper, I could meet him there instead of waiting here. Or I could get back to Sebastian on the street and shake on that barn deal proper. Two hundred deposit puts 1200 more in my hand when the barn's done.

But I'm hungry first. Need food in me before I make any more deals my belly regrets.

"Priorities, Ingram," I say out loud. "Food, then deals, then sleep. The Ingram way."

Let me check where I can actually get a meal. The farmland's close—Sebastian might even be there, and I can kill two birds. Empty farmland, no one there. Sebastian's still on the street then, not working his field. And I need to find actual food—something I can eat today. The grocery store might have something, though the list said bread and flour are out of stock. Let me check what's actually on the shelf, or find someone selling food I can afford.

I could also check The Rose and Crown Pub—pubs usually have meals. Or the temple sometimes has offerings. Let me look at the hospital ward since that's where Lior's headed eventually, and it might have food or at least connections to people who need construction work.

But I'm running out of afternoon, and I need to eat. Let me check what the grocery store has, since I'm listed as having gone there earlier. Browse Farid's grocery store. Jovana's there, Delphine too—the ones running for election, apart from Hendrik. Bread's priced at 35, flour at 10, but the earlier list said none in stock. Let me walk there and see if I can actually buy something, or if I'm just looking at empty shelves again.

Farid runs the place. He chased me earlier while I was busy. No offense, I told him, meaning every word. But I need food, and if he's actually got something on the shelf...

"Right then," I say, standing up from where I'm leaning. "Walk to the grocery, face Farid's temper, and hope he's got more than attitude to sell me."

Let me move there and find out if there's actually anything worth buying.  Good, I'm here. Let me look around and see what's actually on the shelf, and who I'm dealing with.
